Annualized capacity of ~50 million units for Automotive batteries
Total Industrial batteries capacity of 2.3 Billion AH

Lubricants revenue target for FY25 set at over INR150 cr, up from INR25 cr in Q4 FY24
Cell commercial production targeted for latter half of FY26; first revenues expected in FY27
FY24 consolidated capex was ~INR800 cr across recycling, New Energy and lead-acid
Pack facility at Divitipally completed; 1 GWh line to start commercial production next month, adding to existing 0.5 GWh at Tirupati for total 1.5 GWh
Recycling plant under construction with ultimate capacity of 150,000 tonnes per annum, covering ~40% of lead requirement
New Energy business doubled in FY24; pack and charger businesses showing significant traction
Q4 FY24 consolidated EBITDA margin ~14%; adjusted for one-time stamp duty (INR20 cr) and higher trading share, margin would be ~1 percentage point higher
Recycling venture expected to improve material cost by 2-3% and EBITDA margin by 0.5-0.7% at consolidated level
Initial LFP capacity of 4-6 GWh to start; overall 16 GWh cell capacity target over 8-10 years maintained
Capex per GWh expected around INR 600-650 crore; total 16 GWh investment broadly unchanged from earlier INR 9,600 crore estimate

Operating margin improved ~0.6-0.7% YoY due to price increases (1% in June, 0.75% in July) despite higher lead, copper, plastic costs; Q-o-Q margin dilution from higher trading mix (23% vs 12% in Q4)
Lead-acid capex ~INR800 cr (INR450 cr tubular plant, rest line expansions/maintenance); tubular plant completion by end FY25 for next season
New Energy capex: INR2,000 cr for pack facility, customer qualification plant, E Positive labs, 2GW NMC line; LFP 4-5 GWh initial capacity estimated at INR2,000-2,500 cr
Lead-acid capacity: ~21M 4-wheeler and ~32M 2-wheeler batteries at 85-90% utilization; added 5-6% throughput without major capex; line additions planned for 4-wheeler
New Energy: Pack facility commercial production in ~10 days; NMC commercial production end FY26/Q1 FY27; LFP commercial production calendar H2 2027
New Energy revenue grew ~20% YoY driven by mobility and energy storage packs; charger revenue stagnated, expected to grow after localization
No formal volume guidance; industry aftermarket growth estimates: 4-wheeler 7-8%, 2-wheeler 12-13%; company aims to grow faster than market

Management targets 14% operating margin, up from ~13% currently, driven by tubular plant startup, lead recycling, and throughput gains.

Q4 FY25 margins negatively impacted by ~1.5-2% due to higher antimony alloy costs, power cost adjustments, solar settlement delays, higher trading revenue, and additional warranty/employee provisions.
FY25 consolidated capex ~INR1,200 cr: ~INR400 cr tubular reinstatement, ~INR500 cr other lead acid, INR200-300 cr New Energy (qualification plant, R&D lab, gigafactory land).
FY26 capex similar to FY25 (~INR1,200 cr), bulk towards New Energy (~INR1,000 cr) for three projects under construction; cash flow timing may vary 15-20%.
Lead recycling plant started commercial operations in Q4 FY25 with 50,000 MT/yr capacity, scaling to 100,000 MT/yr; refining operational, battery breaking in Q2/Q3 FY26.
Tubular battery plant reinstatement underway, commercial production starting June 2025, reducing trading mix and improving margins.
Throughput enhancement added ~6 million battery capacity without significant capex via Industry 4.0 initiatives.
New Energy: two pack facilities (Tirupati, Hyderabad) with eventual 7 GWh cumulative capacity for telecom, UPS, light EV; R&D facility and customer qualification plant on track for end of CY2025.
First gigafactory broke ground, capacity coming online H1 2027 (~20 GWh ultimate); further capacity tied to firm offtake agreements.
New Energy: two sizable DC fast charger orders from private charge point operators under execution; grid-scale BESS orders won, first external deployments this year.
